full_judgment: 3. The contesting defendant Nos. 1(a) to 1(d), the heirs of Shihamul Haque contested the above suit by tiling written statement denying the claim of the appellants and stating, inter-alia, that Shihamul Haque, his father Enamul Haq and his mother Tahera Sogra Begum, were the inhabitants of Bardwan District in India and after they settled in the then East Pakistan in 1950 migrating from India, Chaturi Tanti along with Shibulal, Bhutu, Surjagaya and Nathuri Tanti proposed to exchange their lands including suit land of the above mouza Chandana with the land of Shamsul Hoque, Enamul Hoque and Tahera Sogra Begum at Bardwan and then a deed of agreement was duly executed which was registered on 30.10.1963 and pursuant to the above agreement the parties handed over the possession of their respective lands to each other acknowledging delivery of possession. Embargo being created upon, the Hindus to transfer their properties by registered deed of conveyances on promulgation of defence of Pakistan Rules several powers of attorney were given to each other by both sides on the basis of which exchange deeds were executed in Bardawan in India and by one of such deed of exchanged dated 09.08.1968 executed in India Tahera Sogra Begum exchanged 1.36 acres of her lands at Bardwan with .89 acres land of Chaturi and Nathuni Tanti of mouza Chandana which includes the suit land. Bhatu Tanti, Chaturi Tanti and 3 others made joint declaration before the Notary Public in Calcutta on 15.07.1968 and 12.08.1968 confirming the above exchange of their lands of mouza Chandana including the suit land. The facts of the execution and registration of the above agreement to exchange in the year 1963, the irrevocable power of attorney and the exchange deeds were duly certified by the Magistrate, First Class, Alipur, West Bengal, India on 17.07.1968 and 10.09.1968. Shihamul Haque applied to the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka praying for permission to execute and register the deed of exchange under the authority of general power of attorney executed in his favour whereupon the above Exchange Case No. 35/69-70 was started. Shibulal Tanti, Chaturi Tanti and others filed an objection in the above exchange case contending, inter alia, they did not enter into any such agreement nor did they exchange their properties and that the exchange deed is fraudulent and powers of attorney are collusive and were vitiated by coercion, threat and intimidation. Shibulal Tanti also filed Title Suit No. 27 of 1971 in the 1st Court of Sub-Judge, Dhaka against Shihamul Haque and others challenging the deed of agreement for exchange, powers of attorney as well as the deed of exchange but the suit was dismissed for non-prosecution and-subsequently he prayed for restoration of the suit which was rejected by order dated 08.06.1972 and thereafter Shibulal Tanti filed Title Suit No. 150 of 1972 in the same court against Shihamul Haque and others seeking same declarations as made in the previous suit and then prayed for amendment which was rejected as the suit filed earlier was dismissed. Against this order of rejection Tanti filed Civil Revision No. 315 of 1977 and also filed Civil Revision No. 1372 of 1977 on more or less similar grounds. Then both the above Rules were discharged on the basis of prayers of Tanti to the effect that they do not want to press the Rules, after the disposal of the above suits/revisions Shihamul Haque applied to Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Dhaka to proceed with the above Exchange Case No. 35 of 1969-70 who then after making necessary, enquiry and after completing all the formalities executed and registered the deed of exchange (Settlement) on 16.06.1980 transferring 7.12 acres of land of mouza Chandana in favour of Shihamul Haque thereafter on the basis of the above deed of exchange Shihamul Haque started Mutation Appeal Case No. 13 of 1981 in the office of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Dhaka, praying for canceling the earlier mutation in the name of the appellant and got the mutation cancelled. The subsequent order as stated earlier were passed by the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka in Appeal Case No. 8 of 1982, the Board of Land Administration in Appeal No. 86 of 1984 and the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 159 of 1980 made the Rule absolute with the observation that the question of title and validity of the deed of exchange could be decided only by the civil court. The defendants have been possessing the suit land along with other lands by cultivating and growing crops therein through bargadars namely Kamal's mother and her son-in-law.
